assumptions.condition: For every \(s\in\mathcal S\), \(M^s\) is a recursive finite-state SCM compatible with \(G\) on \(\mathcal X\).
In every domain \(s\), the exogenous response blocks associated with distinct elements of \(\mathcal D(G)\) are mutually independent.
For every \(s\in\mathcal S\) and \(D\in\mathcal D(G)\) with \(D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing\), the joint law of the structural response maps on \(D\) in \(M^s\) equals its law in \(M^\star\).

novel.justification: A shared laboratory pipeline, record-linkage platform, or policy module can preserve the entire latent response block for a confounded district across sites. This is deliberately stronger than ordinary vertex-level selection-diagram invariance because Layer-3 laws depend on cross-world coupling inside the district.

assumptions.condition: For every \(s\in\mathcal S\) and \(D\in\mathcal D(G)\), either \(D\subseteq\Delta_s\) or \(D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing\).

novel.justification: Site changes often act on an entire confounded measurement or policy block. Whole-district selection permits arbitrary changes inside that block while ruling out an unsupported splice of cross-world dependence across only part of it.

assumptions.condition: For every \(s\in\mathcal S\) and \(a\in\mathcal A_s\), \(P_a^s\) equals the law induced by regime \(a\) in \(M^s\).
For every \(D\in\mathcal D(G)\), the bidirected subgraph induced by \(D\) is complete.

For every \(s\in\mathcal S\) and \(D\in\mathcal D(G)\), all mechanisms on \(D\) are generated by one finite latent variable \(U_D^s\in\Omega_D^{\mathrm{all}}\), where \(\Omega_D^{\mathrm{all}}\) contains the deterministic response maps at every parent configuration: if \(U_D^s=\omega_D=(f_V:V\in D)\), then the structural equation of each \(V\in D\) reads the component \(f_V\); the variables \((U_D^s:D\in\mathcal D(G))\) are mutually independent.

definitions.name: District-closed finite transport class
definitions.construction: \[\mathfrak M(G,\mathcal X,\mathcal S,\{\Delta_s\}_{s\in\mathcal S})=\{\mathbf M=(M^s:s\in\mathcal S):\mathbf M\text{ is recursively compatible, district-factorized, district-kernel invariant, and district-closed}\}.\]

definitions.name: Typed-menu compatibility fiber
definitions.construction: \[\mathcal C(\mathcal P)=\{\mathbf M\in\mathfrak M(G,\mathcal X,\mathcal S,\{\Delta_s\}_{s\in\mathcal S}):P_{M^s}^{a}=P_a^s\text{ for every }s\in\mathcal S,\ a\in\mathcal A_s\}.\]

definitions.name: Canonical district response profile
definitions.construction: For each \(D\in\mathcal D(G)\), enumerate every tuple of deterministic maps \(\omega_D=(f_V:V\in D)\) on the parent configurations visited by \(B_\rho\), \(E\), and \(\mathcal P\); the resulting finite set is \(\Omega_D\), and \(q_D^s(\omega_D)=P_{M^s}(\omega_D)\).

definitions.name: Certified typed extraction judgment
definitions.construction: For \(P_a^s\in\Delta(\mathcal X_{W_a})\), write \[\operatorname{Extract}_{s,a,D}(P_a^s)\Downarrow(K_{s,a,D},\kappa)\] exactly when consistency, unnesting, ancestor restriction, fixing, and marginalization define a kernel \(K_{s,a,D}:H_{s,a,D}\to\Delta(C_{s,a,D})\) and \(\kappa\in\mathscr R(\mathcal P)\) certifies every context, marginal, and nonzero divisor used. An undefined fixing, unavailable context, or uncertified quotient has no successful judgment.

definitions.name: Context-indexed extracted-cell incidence row
definitions.construction: \[r_{s,a,D,h,c}(\omega_D)=\mathbf 1\{\omega_D\text{ produces extracted cell }c\text{ at context }h\text{ under regime }a\},\qquad\omega_D\in\Omega_D.\]

definitions.name: Source-labelled lossless stacked district system
definitions.construction:
For each complete supplied cell \(C_{a,v}\) in domain \(s\), first prove the transport-admissibility predicate \(s=\star\) or \(D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing\).  If recursive evaluation of \(C_{a,v}\) visits only \(D\), retain before all derived rows the raw identity-extraction row
\[
r^{\mathrm{raw}}_{s,a,D,v}(\omega_D)=\mathbf 1\{C_{a,v}\text{ is true under }\omega_D\},
\qquad \omega_D\in\Omega_D,
\]
with value \(P_a^s(v)\).  Thus every transport-admissible complete-menu cell whose reduction is district-local is retained even when no nontrivial fixing quotient is available.  Next, for every successful judgment \(\operatorname{Extract}_{s,a,D}(P_a^s)\Downarrow(K_{s,a,D},\kappa)\) with the same admissibility proof, retain every available row \(r_{s,a,D,h,c}\) and value \(K_{s,a,D}(c\mid h)\).  Prepend \(\mathbf 1^\top\), stack the normalization row, raw rows, and derived rows in canonical order as \(A_D\), and stack their values as \(m_D\).  A failed derived extraction creates no derived row, but it does not delete an independently certified raw district-local row.  A changed-district source cell and a cell whose recursive indicator depends on more than \(D\) create no row in \(A_D\); their complete equalities remain in the global response-profile or graph-compatible canonical fiber.

definitions.name: District row face and global projections
definitions.construction:
Define the district row face and its forced-zero coordinates by
\[
\mathcal K_D(m_D)=\{q\in\mathbb R_{\ge0}^{\Omega_D}:A_Dq=m_D\},
\qquad
Z_D(m_D)=\{\omega\in\Omega_D:q(\omega)=0\text{ for every }q\in\mathcal K_D(m_D)\}.
\]
Define the broad and saturated global district projections by
\[
\mathcal Q_D(\mathcal P)=\{q_D^\star(\mathbf M):\mathbf M\in\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\},
\qquad
\mathcal Q_D^{\mathrm{sat}}(\mathcal P)=\{q_D^\star(\mathbf M):\mathbf M\in\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat}}(\mathcal P)\}.
\]

definitions.name: Common-evidence arm row system
definitions.construction: Reduce \(B_\rho\cap E\) and \(E\) to target-district cells and evaluate them on \(\Omega_D\), obtaining \(n_{\rho,D}\) and \(d_D\); set \(g_{\rho,\sigma,D}=n_{\sigma,D}-n_{\rho,D}\). The same reduction applied to any target cell gives \(b_D\).

definitions.name: Sharp transported dominance margin
definitions.construction: \[\Gamma_{\rho\prec\sigma}(m_D)=\min_{q\in\mathcal K_D(m_D)}g_{\rho,\sigma,D}q,\qquad \overline\Gamma_{\rho\prec\sigma}(m_D)=\max_{q\in\mathcal K_D(m_D)}g_{\rho,\sigma,D}q.\]

definitions.name: Menu-dual dominance certificate
definitions.construction: A certificate at level \(\gamma\in\mathbb R\) is a vector \(\eta_{\rho,\sigma,D}\) satisfying \(A_D^\top\eta_{\rho,\sigma,D}\le g_{\rho,\sigma,D}^\top\) coordinatewise and \(m_D^\top\eta_{\rho,\sigma,D}\ge\gamma\).

definitions.name: One-cell Layer-3 sign-regime frontier
definitions.construction: \[I_D=\{r_D^\dagger q:q\in\mathcal K_D(m_D)\},\qquad\Gamma_{\rho\prec\sigma}(p;m_D)=\min_{\substack{q\in\mathcal K_D(m_D)\\ r_D^\dagger q=p}}g_{\rho,\sigma,D}q,\qquad\mathcal J_{\rho\prec\sigma}^+=\{p\in I_D:\Gamma_{\rho\prec\sigma}(p;m_D)>0\}.\]

definitions.name: Finite ex-post regime-block acquisition problem
definitions.construction: For each realizable experiment \(e\in\mathcal U\), the dependent block \((R_e,p_e)\) is revealed jointly at cost \(c_e>0\). For \(S\subseteq\mathcal U\), define \[\mathcal K_S=\{q\in\mathcal K_D(m_D):R_eq=p_e\text{ for every }e\in S\},\qquad \operatorname{PO}(S)=\{\rho:\exists q\in\mathcal K_S,\ \forall\sigma\in\mathcal R_{\mathrm{arm}},\ Q_\rho(q)\ge Q_\sigma(q)\},\] \[\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}}=\operatorname{PO}(\mathcal U),\qquad \min_{S\subseteq\mathcal U}\sum_{e\in S}c_e\quad\text{subject to}\quad\operatorname{PO}(S)=\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}},\qquad f(S)=\lvert\mathcal R_{\mathrm{arm}}\rvert-\lvert\operatorname{PO}(S)\rvert.\]

definitions.name: Complete binary acquisition and strictness instance
definitions.construction: Let \(\mathfrak I_{\mathrm{bin}}\) have binary \(T_{\mathrm{tr}}\to Y\) and isolated binary \(Z\), target \(\star\), source \(s\), and \(\Delta_s=\{Z\}\), so the invariant district is \(D=\{Y\}\). Set \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{arm}}=\{\rho,\sigma\}\), \(E=\top\), \(B_\rho=\{(Y_0,Y_1):Y_0\ne Y_1\}\), \(B_\sigma=\{(Y_0,Y_1):Y_1=1\}\), and \(\mathcal U=\{e^\dagger\}\). Order \(\Omega_D=\{(0,0),(0,1),(1,0),(1,1)\}\) for \((Y_0,Y_1)\), and set \[A_D=\begin{bmatrix}1&1&1&1\\0&0&1&1\\0&1&0&1\end{bmatrix},\quad m_D=(1,1/2,1/2)^\top,\quad \mathcal K_D(m_D)=\{q(p)=(p,1/2-p,1/2-p,p):0\le p\le1/2\},\quad Z_D(m_D)=\varnothing.\] The event incidence rows are \(n_{\rho,D}=(0,1,1,0)\), \(n_{\sigma,D}=(0,1,0,1)\), and \(d_D=(1,1,1,1)\), so \(g_{\rho,\sigma,D}=(0,0,-1,1)\). The sole block has \(c_{e^\dagger}=1\), \(R_{e^\dagger}=r_D^\dagger=(0,0,0,1)\), and reveals the genuine Layer-3 source cell \(p_{e^\dagger}=p=P^s(Y_0=1,Y_1=1)=3/8\). Also set \(P^\star(Z=1)=0\) and \(P^s(Z=1)=1\).

definitions.name: Allowed rational functional
definitions.construction: \(\mathscr R(\mathcal P)\) is the typed expression-and-certificate algebra generated from menu cells by finite sums, differences, products, marginalization sums, and quotients carrying a proof that the divisor is nonzero on the relevant compatibility fiber.

definitions.name: DCTFTR syntax, configurations, and terminals
definitions.construction:
Fix canonical finite orders on vertices, regimes, districts, assignments, and generated DAG-node identifiers. The event grammar is \[\mathsf{Atom}::=[s]\,V_{\alpha}=v,\qquad \mathsf{Event}::=	op\mid ot\mid\mathsf{Atom}\mid\mathsf{Event}\wedge\mathsf{Event}\mid\mathsf{Event}\vee\mathsf{Event},\] where \(\alpha\) is a finite well-typed intervention or partial-copy term and canonical normalized events are disjoint normal forms of unnested atoms. Identified expressions have grammar \[\mathsf{Expr}::=\operatorname{Cell}(s,a,u)\mid\operatorname{Rat}(r)\mid\sum_{j\in J}\mathsf{Expr}_j\mid\prod_{j\in J}\mathsf{Expr}_j\mid\operatorname{Quot}(F,G,
u_G),\] where \(r\in\mathbb Q\) and \(
u_G\) is an independently checked nonzero certificate. The phase-indexed node grammar is exactly \[\mathsf{Goal}::=\operatorname{Raw}(	au,e)\mid\operatorname{Normed}(	au,e,
u)\mid\operatorname{AncClosed}(	au,H,e,\alpha)\mid\operatorname{NeedRows}(	au,D,b)\mid\operatorname{NeedFace}(	au,D,b,A,m,Z,\kappa)\mid\operatorname{Sum}(J,\mathrm{children})\mid\operatorname{Prod}(\mathrm{children})\mid\operatorname{Resolved}(F,\delta),\] with \(	au\in\{\mathrm{num},\mathrm{den}\}\). A configuration is a finite well-typed acyclic work DAG of these nodes, its numerator and denominator roots, and a checked trace. For every \(\mathbf M\in\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\), node denotation is defined recursively: the first three event phases denote their target event probability; \(\operatorname{NeedRows}(	au,D,b)\) and \(\operatorname{NeedFace}(	au,D,b,A,m,Z,\kappa)\) denote \(bq_D^\star(\mathbf M)\); \(\operatorname{Resolved}(F,\delta)\) denotes \(F(\mathcal P)\); and sum and product nodes denote the corresponding finite sum and product of child denotations. Configuration denotation is the ordered pair of root values. Checked derivations are finite syntax trees: normalization derivations use only consistency, unnesting, contradiction, Boolean normalization, and finite disjoint-additivity constructors; ancestor derivations enumerate summed assignments; district-split derivations enumerate the districts of \(G[H]\) and use finite marginalization and semi-Markovian district factorization; extraction derivations record each fixing, marginalization, context lookup, and certified quotient; face certificates are exact rational LP or Farkas certificates; and zero, nonzero, or strict-positivity certificates are checked by exact rational ring normalization together with Farkas certificates for linear face constraints or displayed sum-of-squares preordering identities for the finite response-law constraints. Thus no certificate constructor consists merely of the semantic equality or inequality being certified. The terminals are \[\mathsf{Result}::=\operatorname{ID}(F,\delta)\mid\operatorname{ZERO\_EVIDENCE}(F_E,z)\mid\operatorname{FAIL}(t),\] where a conditioning derivation \(\delta\) records the numerator derivation, denominator derivation, and positivity certificate. Failure constructors include \(\operatorname{SPLIT\_UNDEFINED}(v,\mathrm{reason},t)\), \(\operatorname{EXTRACTION\_UNDEFINED}(s,a,D,h)\), \(\operatorname{FACE\_NOT\_IDENTIFIED}(D,b,A,m,Z,w_{\mathrm{local}},t)\), \(\operatorname{NO\_ADMISSIBLE\_FACTOR}(D,b,\mathrm{retainedRows},t)\), \(\operatorname{DENOMINATOR\_MAY\_VANISH}(E,\mathbf M,t)\), \(\operatorname{DENOMINATOR\_POSITIVITY\_UNCERTIFIED}(E,t)\), and \(\operatorname{STUCK}(\mathrm{phase},\mathrm{reason},t)\).

definitions.name: District-closed Layer-3 transport recursion
definitions.construction:
Initialize one finite acyclic work DAG with roots \(\operatorname{Raw}(\mathrm{num},B_ho\wedge E)\) and \(\operatorname{Raw}(\mathrm{den},E)\); its denotation at \(\mathbf M\in\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\) is \((P_{M^\star}(B_ho\wedge E),P_{M^\star}(E))\). The deterministic transition system \(\mathsf{DCTFTR}\) has these eight rules. \(\mathsf{NORM}\): replace the least \(\operatorname{Raw}(	au,e)\) by \(\operatorname{Normed}(	au,\operatorname{nf}(e),
u)\), where the total finite-state checker applies consistency, unnesting, contradiction removal, and disjoint-normal-form rewriting and returns a derivation \(
u:P(e)=P(\operatorname{nf}(e))\); append \(\operatorname{NORM}(v,e,\operatorname{nf}(e),
u)\). \(\mathsf{ANCESTOR}\): for the least normalized node, enumerate its counterfactual ancestors \(H\), the assignments summed out, and a checked finite marginalization derivation \(\alpha\), then replace it by \(\operatorname{AncClosed}(	au,H,e|_H,\alpha)\) and append \(\operatorname{ANCESTOR}(v,H,\alpha)\). \(\mathsf{SPLIT}\): for the least ancestor-closed node, the compiler mechanically enumerates \(G[H]\), its districts, and all finite summation assignments and builds an acyclic sum-product DAG with leaves \(\operatorname{NeedRows}(	au,D,b)\); its checker constructs \(\sigma\) from finite marginalization and district-factorization rules, the DAG is spliced in, and \(\operatorname{SPLIT}(v,D_1,\ldots,D_k,\sigma)\) is appended. If enumeration or typing is undefined, return \(\operatorname{FAIL}(\operatorname{SPLIT\_UNDEFINED}(v,\mathrm{reason},t))\). \(\mathsf{EXTRACT}\): at the least \(\operatorname{NeedRows}(	au,D,b)\), enumerate all supplied \((s,a)\) and their complete cells canonically.  After a checked proof of \(s=\star\) or \(D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing\), first retain every complete cell whose recursive indicator visits only \(D\) as the raw equality \(P_a^s(v)=r^{\mathrm{raw}}_{s,a,D,v}q_D^\star\).  Then retain a derived context and cell only when \(\operatorname{Extract}_{s,a,D}(P_a^s)\Downarrow(K_{s,a,D},\kappa)\) succeeds with the same admissibility proof; the recomputed extraction tree must prove \(K_{s,a,D}(c\mid h)=r_{s,a,D,h,c}q_D^\star\). Record every failed derived extraction, changed-district rejection, and cross-district raw cell without turning it into a district row. Prepend the normalization row, stack accepted raw and derived rows and values canonically as \((A_D,m_D)\), even if no non-normalization row survives, replace the node by \(\operatorname{NeedFace}(	au,D,b,A_D,m_D,Z_D(m_D),\kappa_{\mathrm{all}})\), and append the accepted rows, rejected candidates, admissibility proofs, and derivations; \(\kappa_{\mathrm{all}}\) checks \(A_Dq_D^\star=m_D\). \(\mathsf{FACE\_ID}\): for the least face node, compute \(Z=\{\omega:q(\omega)=0	ext{ for every }q\ge0	ext{ with }Aq=m\}\), with an exact LP or Farkas certificate for every coordinate, and test \(b\in\operatorname{row}(A)+\operatorname{span}\{e_\omega:\omega\in Z\}\). If membership holds, fixed-pivot reduced row echelon form chooses \(b=\lambda^	op A+\sum_{\omega\in Z}\zeta_\omega e_\omega\); replace the node by \(\operatorname{Resolved}(\lambda^	op m,\delta_{\mathrm{face}})\), where the checker verifies \(bq=\lambda^	op Aq+\sum_{\omega\in Z}\zeta_\omega q(\omega)=\lambda^	op m\), and append the certificates. If membership fails, return \(\operatorname{FAIL}(\operatorname{FACE\_NOT\_IDENTIFIED}(D,b,A,m,Z,w_{\mathrm{local}},t))\); \(w_{\mathrm{local}}\) witnesses only variation in the district row relaxation.  It is not a pair of globally compatible SCMs unless district saturation and the district-separated one-district projection hypotheses have been checked. If no non-normalization raw or derived row succeeded, use \(\operatorname{NO\_ADMISSIBLE\_FACTOR}\) instead only after this normalization-only face test fails. \(\mathsf{MARGINALIZE}\): replace the least ready \(\operatorname{Sum}(J,\mathrm{children})\), all of whose children are resolved, by \(\operatorname{Resolved}(\sum_{j\in J}F_j,\delta_{\mathrm{sum}})\), using finite additivity and child derivations. \(\mathsf{PRODUCT}\): replace the least ready product node by \(\operatorname{Resolved}(\prod_jF_j,\delta_{\mathrm{prod}})\), using district factorization and child derivations. \(\mathsf{CONDITION}\): when both roots are \(\operatorname{Resolved}(F_B,\delta_B)\) and \(\operatorname{Resolved}(F_E,\delta_E)\), append a condition record and return \(\operatorname{ZERO\_EVIDENCE}(F_E,z)\) if the independent zero calculus proves \(F_E=0\) throughout \(\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\); return \(\operatorname{ID}(\operatorname{Quot}(F_B,F_E,\pi),\delta_B,\delta_E,\pi)\) if the independent positivity calculus proves \(F_E>0\) throughout that fiber; return \(\operatorname{FAIL}(\operatorname{DENOMINATOR\_MAY\_VANISH}(E,\mathbf M,t))\) if an explicitly checked \(\mathbf M\in\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\) has \(F_E=0\); otherwise return \(\operatorname{FAIL}(\operatorname{DENOMINATOR\_POSITIVITY\_UNCERTIFIED}(E,t))\). Rule priority is \(\mathsf{NORM}>\mathsf{ANCESTOR}>\mathsf{SPLIT}>\mathsf{EXTRACT}>\mathsf{FACE\_ID}>\mathsf{MARGINALIZE}>\mathsf{PRODUCT}>\mathsf{CONDITION}\); within a rule choose the least applicable node, where applicability includes readiness. No rule creates an earlier-phase node. For nonterminals, \(\operatorname{rank}_{\mathrm{lex}}=(r_N,r_A,r_S,r_X,r_F,r_{\Sigma},r_{\Pi},r_C)\): the rules respectively decrease the indicated first still-changeable coordinate, with \(\mathsf{CONDITION}\) changing \(r_C=1\) to zero after the first seven coordinates vanish; later coordinates may increase. If no rule applies to a nonterminal, return \(\operatorname{FAIL}(\operatorname{STUCK}(\mathrm{phase},\mathrm{reason},t))\).

definitions.name: Cross-menu face-preservation handle
definitions.construction: \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{preserve}}\) starts from the exact feasible face \(\mathcal K_D(m_D)\) and tracks both its affine hull and forced-zero coordinates through ancestor restriction, fixing, district splitting, and marginalization in \(\mathsf{DCTFTR}\).

definitions.name: Layer-3 menu-acquisition handle
definitions.construction: \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{acquire}}\) enumerates realizable regime blocks \((R_e,p_e)\), propagates each full dependent block through the finite dual bases defining arm values on \(\mathcal K_S\), and solves the finite ex-post covering problem \(\min_{S\subseteq\mathcal U}\sum_{e\in S}c_e\) subject to \(\operatorname{PO}(S)=\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}}\).

definitions.name: Partial-district invariance-frontier handle
definitions.construction: \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{leak}}\) splits a selected district response kernel across \(D\cap\Delta_s\) and \(D\setminus\Delta_s\), tests whether supplied and target Layer-3 factors depend on a common invariant marginal kernel, and searches the smallest binary crossing perturbation when they do not.

definitions.name: Exact saturated response-profile and sparse canonical fibers
definitions.construction:
For a response-profile tuple \(\theta=(q_D^s:s\in\mathcal S,\ D\in\mathcal D(G))\) with \(q_D^s\in\Delta(\Omega_D)\), define, for every finite counterfactual cell \(C\),
\[
\Psi_C^s(\theta^s)=
\sum_{\omega\in\prod_{D\in\mathcal D(G)}\Omega_D}
\mathbf 1\{C\text{ is true under recursive evaluation of }\omega\}
\prod_{D\in\mathcal D(G)}q_D^s(\omega_D).
\]
If the recursive indicator of \(C\) depends on the profiles in \(k\) districts, then \(\Psi_C^s\) is multi-affine in the district probability blocks and has total degree at most \(k\).  Writing \(C_{a,v}\) for the complete cell in which descriptor \(a\) returns \(v\in\mathcal X_{W_a}\), define the saturated response-profile fiber
\[
\begin{split}
\Theta(\mathcal P)=\bigl\{\theta:{}&q_D^s\in\Delta(\Omega_D)
\quad(s\in\mathcal S,\ D\in\mathcal D(G)),\\
&q_D^s=q_D^\star\quad\text{if }D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing,\\
&\Psi_{C_{a,v}}^s(\theta^s)=P_a^s(v)
\quad\text{for every }s\in\mathcal S,\ a\in\mathcal A_s,
\ v\in\mathcal X_{W_a}\bigr\}.
\end{split}
\]
For a target cell \(T\), set
\[
L_T(\mathcal P)=\min_{\theta\in\Theta(\mathcal P)}\Psi_T^\star(\theta^\star),
\qquad
U_T(\mathcal P)=\max_{\theta\in\Theta(\mathcal P)}\Psi_T^\star(\theta^\star),
\]
and define
\[
\mathcal G_{\rho,\sigma}(\theta)
=\Psi_{B_\sigma\cap E}^\star(\theta^\star)
-\Psi_{B_\rho\cap E}^\star(\theta^\star).
\]

For an arbitrary, possibly nonsaturated ADMG \(G\), retain a separate graph-compatible canonical parameter \(\vartheta^s=(\mu^s,p^s)\in\operatorname{Can}(G,\mathcal X)\).  Its simplex and one-hot coordinates satisfy
\[
p_U^s(u)\geq0,\qquad \sum_up_U^s(u)=1,
\qquad \mu_{V,v\mid pa,u_V}^s\in\{0,1\},
\qquad \sum_{v\in\mathcal X_V}\mu_{V,v\mid pa,u_V}^s=1,
\]
with the graph-compatible latent-factor restrictions and product law across distinct districts retained.  Let \(\Phi_{C,\mathrm{can}}^s(\vartheta^s)\) be the finite recursive canonical cell polynomial and let \(q_{D,\mathrm{can}}^s(\cdot;\vartheta^s)\) be its induced joint response-profile law on \(D\).  Define
\[
\begin{split}
\Theta_G^{\mathrm{can}}(\mathcal P)=\bigl\{\vartheta:{}&
\vartheta^s\in\operatorname{Can}(G,\mathcal X)\quad(s\in\mathcal S),\\
&q_{D,\mathrm{can}}^s(\cdot;\vartheta^s)=q_{D,\mathrm{can}}^\star(\cdot;\vartheta^\star)
\quad\text{if }D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing,\\
&\Phi_{C_{a,v},\mathrm{can}}^s(\vartheta^s)=P_a^s(v)
\quad\text{for every complete supplied cell}\bigr\}.
\end{split}
\]
The first fiber deliberately uses district-saturated response-block semantics; the second retains all internal latent-factor restrictions of a sparse \(G\).

definitions.name: Saturated typed-menu compatibility fiber
definitions.construction:
\[
\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat}}(\mathcal P)=\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\cap\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{sat}}(G,\mathcal X,\mathcal S,\{\Delta_s\}_{s\in\mathcal S}).
\]

definitions.name: District-separated complete-menu condition
definitions.construction: For \(D\in\mathcal D(G)\), the predicate \(\mathsf{Sep}_D(\mathcal P)\) holds when every complete supplied cell \(C_{a,v}\) in a domain satisfying \(s=\star\) or \(D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing\) has, under recursive evaluation on \(\prod_{D'\in\mathcal D(G)}\Omega_{D'}\), an indicator that is either independent of \(\omega_D\), or depends only on \(\omega_D\).  In the second case its raw row \(r^{\mathrm{raw}}_{s,a,D,v}\) and value \(P_a^s(v)\) must occur in \((A_D,m_D)\).  This is a finite syntactic and tabular condition; it excludes an unrecorded cross-district polynomial constraint involving \(q_D^\star\).

definitions.name: District-saturated response-block transport subclass
definitions.construction:
Define
\[
\begin{split}
\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{sat}}(G,\mathcal X,\mathcal S,\{\Delta_s\}_{s\in\mathcal S})
=\bigl\{\mathbf M\in\mathfrak M(G,\mathcal X,\mathcal S,\{\Delta_s\}_{s\in\mathcal S}):{}&
G[D]\text{ is bidirected complete for every }D\in\mathcal D(G);\\
&\text{for every }s\in\mathcal S\text{ and }D\in\mathcal D(G),
\text{ exactly one finite latent block }U_D^s\text{ taking values in }\Omega_D^{\mathrm{all}}\\
&\text{stores one full deterministic response map for every vertex in }D
\text{ at every parent configuration};\\
&\text{each structural equation in }D\text{ reads the corresponding component of }U_D^s;\\
&(U_D^s:D\in\mathcal D(G))\text{ are mutually independent within each domain }s;\\
&\text{the class contains every independent choice of one probability law on }
\Omega_D^{\mathrm{all}}\text{ for each permitted district block},\\
&\text{subject only to equality of the laws of }U_D^s\text{ and }U_D^\star
\text{ whenever }D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing\bigr\}.
\end{split}
\]
Thus changed districts may use arbitrary and mutually unrelated response-block laws, unchanged districts use exactly the target response-block law, and no equality with the broad sparse-ADMG class \(\mathfrak M\) is asserted.

definitions.name: Focal-district-saturated response-block transport subclass and fiber
definitions.construction:
For a fixed district \(D\in\mathcal D(G)\), define
\[
\begin{split}
\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{sat},D}(G,\mathcal X,\mathcal S,\{\Delta_s\}_{s\in\mathcal S})
=\bigl\{\mathbf M\in\mathfrak M(G,\mathcal X,\mathcal S,\{\Delta_s\}_{s\in\mathcal S}):{}&
G[D]\text{ is bidirected complete};\\
&\text{for every }s\in\mathcal S\text{ there is exactly one finite latent block }
U_D^s\in\Omega_D^{\mathrm{all}}\\
&\text{storing one full deterministic response map for each vertex in }D
\text{ at every allowed parent configuration};\\
&\text{each structural equation of a vertex in }D
\text{ reads the corresponding component of }U_D^s;\\
&U_D^s\text{ is independent of the exogenous blocks of every }D'\ne D;\\
&\text{every probability law on }\Omega_D^{\mathrm{all}}\text{ is permitted for }U_D^s,
\text{ subject only to equality with the target law}\\
&\text{when }D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing;\\
&\text{for each }D'\ne D\text{, all structural tables, latent-factor restrictions,}
\text{ and cross-domain equalities remain those of }\mathfrak M
\bigr\}.
\end{split}
\]
The phrase ``every probability law is permitted'' includes closure under replacing the law of \(U_D^\star\) and all its unchanged-source copies while holding all mechanisms and latent laws in districts \(D'\ne D\), and all changed-source copies of \(U_D\), fixed. Define
\[
\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)
=\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\cap
\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{sat},D}(G,\mathcal X,\mathcal S,\{\Delta_s\}_{s\in\mathcal S})
\]
and
\[
\mathcal Q_D^{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)
=\{q_D^\star(\mathbf M):\mathbf M\in\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)\}.
\]

definitions.name: Active-slice face-separation condition
definitions.construction:
For a fixed district \(D\), define its active row space by
\[
R_D(m_D)=\operatorname{row}(A_D)+
\operatorname{span}\{e_\omega:\omega\in Z_D(m_D)\}
\subseteq\mathbb R^{\Omega_D}.
\]
For a complete supplied cell \(C_{a,v}\) in domain \(s\) that is transport-admissible for \(D\), meaning \(s=\star\) or \(D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing\), and for
\(\omega_{-D}\in\prod_{D'\in\mathcal D(G),\,D'\ne D}\Omega_{D'}\), define its focal recursive-indicator slice by
\[
\chi_{C_{a,v},\omega_{-D}}(\omega_D)
=\mathbf 1\{C_{a,v}\text{ is true under recursive evaluation of }
(\omega_D,\omega_{-D})\},
\qquad \omega_D\in\Omega_D.
\]
The active-slice face-separation predicate \(\mathsf{ASep}_D(\mathcal P)\) holds exactly when
\[
\chi_{C_{a,v},\omega_{-D}}\in R_D(m_D)
\]
for every transport-admissible complete supplied cell and every fixed nonfocal response profile \(\omega_{-D}\).  When \(D\) is the only district, the nonfocal product is the singleton empty profile.

definitions.name: Baseline-averaged active-slice separation
definitions.construction:
Fix \(D\in\mathcal D(G)\).  For a baseline \(\mathbf M^0\in\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)\), let
\[
\nu_{-D}^{0,s}(\omega_{-D})
=\prod_{D'\in\mathcal D(G),\,D'\ne D}q_{D'}^{0,s}(\omega_{D'}),
\qquad
\omega_{-D}\in\prod_{D'\ne D}\Omega_{D'},
\]
where \(q_{D'}^{0,s}\) is the response-profile law induced by \(M^{0,s}\).  For every complete supplied cell \(C_{a,v}\) in a domain \(s\) that is transport-admissible for \(D\), meaning \(s=\star\) or \(D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing\), define the baseline-averaged focal row
\[
\bar\chi_{C_{a,v}}^{s,\mathbf M^0}
=\sum_{\omega_{-D}}
\nu_{-D}^{0,s}(\omega_{-D})
\chi_{C_{a,v},\omega_{-D}}
\in\mathbb R^{\Omega_D}.
\]
The baseline-averaged active-slice predicate \(\mathsf{BASep}_D(\mathcal P)\) holds exactly when there exists one \(\mathbf M^0\in\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)\) such that
\[
\bar\chi_{C_{a,v}}^{s,\mathbf M^0}\in R_D(m_D)
\]
for every transport-admissible complete supplied cell.  The same witnessing baseline must be used for all cells and all feasible replacements of the focal law; a baseline depending on the replacement law is not permitted.

statements.statement: If \(\operatorname{Extract}_{s,a,D}(P_a^s)\Downarrow(K_{s,a,D},\kappa)\), then for every available \(h\in H_{s,a,D}\) and \(c\in C_{s,a,D}\), \[K_{s,a,D}(c\mid h)=r_{s,a,D,h,c}q_D^s.\] After, and only after, proving \(s=\star\) or \(D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing\), district-kernel invariance gives \(K_{s,a,D}(c\mid h)=r_{s,a,D,h,c}q_D^\star\). The target arm numerator, evidence, and generic target cells equal \(n_{\rho,D}q_D^\star\), \(d_Dq_D^\star\), and \(b_Dq_D^\star\), respectively. Failed extraction yields no incidence row.
statements.justification: This converts every heterogeneous Layer-3 input and each target arm comparison into exact linear information on a fixed response carrier.
statements.gap: Zhang, Tian, and Bareinboim give canonical response carriers, while CTFIDU+ extracts Layer-3 factors; neither gives a source-labelled common-evidence row system under district-level transport.
statements.consumer: The row representation supplies the primal and dual programs used by the face-aware identification and arm-ordering certificates.

statements.statement:
For every district \(D\),
\[
\mathcal Q_D(\mathcal P)\subseteq\mathcal K_D(m_D).
\]
Suppose \(\mathsf{BASep}_D(\mathcal P)\) holds.  This predicate entails \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)\ne\varnothing\), and
\[
\mathcal Q_D^{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)=\mathcal K_D(m_D).
\]
Moreover,
\[
R_D(m_D)
=\operatorname{span}\{q-q':q,q'\in\mathcal K_D(m_D)\}^{\perp}.
\]
For the single witnessing baseline \(\mathbf M^0\) in \(\mathsf{BASep}_D(\mathcal P)\), every transport-admissible complete supplied cell is preserved under replacement of its focal law \(q_0\) by an arbitrary \(q\in\mathcal K_D(m_D)\) because
\[
\bar\chi_{C_{a,v}}^{s,\mathbf M^0}(q-q_0)=0.
\]
Every boundary point of the row face is therefore induced on the declared alphabets \(\mathcal X\) by a compatible SCM family saturated only at \(D\), while every district \(D'\ne D\) retains its original graph-compatible restrictions.  Nonemptiness of \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)\) together with \(\mathsf{ASep}_D(\mathcal P)\), and hence also together with \(\mathsf{Sep}_D(\mathcal P)\), is a convenient sufficient condition for \(\mathsf{BASep}_D(\mathcal P)\).  Without baseline-averaged separation or focal-district saturation, only the displayed broad inclusion is asserted.
statements.justification: The equality is the causal realization step making focal-district optimization sharp whenever one compatible baseline preserves all complete-menu cells through their averaged focal rows.
statements.gap: Existing Layer-3 completeness results do not give this heterogeneous fixed-alphabet projection theorem or isolate the weaker baseline-averaged condition from pointwise slice separation.
statements.consumer: Every local optimizer becomes an explicit compatible SCM while all nonfocal districts retain their graph-compatible baseline restrictions.

statements.statement:
For the broad compatibility fiber, membership in the active row space,
\[
b_D\in R_D(m_D)
=\operatorname{row}(A_D)+\operatorname{span}\{e_\omega:\omega\in Z_D(m_D)\},
\]
is sufficient for the district-local target \(b_Dq_D^\star\) to be identified, with value \(\lambda^\top m_D\) whenever
\[
b_D=\lambda^\top A_D+\sum_{\omega\in Z_D(m_D)}\zeta_\omega e_\omega.
\]
If additionally \(\mathsf{BASep}_D(\mathcal P)\) holds, membership is also necessary for constancy on \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)\).  On that focal-district-saturated baseline-averaged class, failure yields two compatible SCM families on the original alphabets \(\mathcal X\) that agree on every supplied law and disagree on the target cell, while every district \(D'\ne D\) retains its original graph-compatible restrictions.  Nonemptiness of \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)\) together with \(\mathsf{ASep}_D(\mathcal P)\), and hence with \(\mathsf{Sep}_D(\mathcal P)\), is sufficient for this exact clause.  For a problem outside the baseline-averaged focal-projection scope, failure is only a local outer-relaxation witness.
statements.justification: Forced-zero coordinates give broad identification and, under exact single-baseline focal projection, a necessary fixed-alphabet criterion with paired countermodels.
statements.gap: Published Layer-3 identification does not provide this boundary-face row-space characterization or the weaker baseline-averaged source-labelled realization condition.
statements.consumer: Menus that preserve cross-district cells only after averaging under a compatible baseline can identify targets and certify nonidentification beyond pointwise slice tests.

statements.statement: For every \(\mathbf M\in\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\), each nonterminal \(\mathsf{NORM}\), \(\mathsf{ANCESTOR}\), \(\mathsf{SPLIT}\), \(\mathsf{EXTRACT}\), \(\mathsf{FACE\_ID}\), \(\mathsf{MARGINALIZE}\), or \(\mathsf{PRODUCT}\) step preserves the ordered pair of root denotations pointwise. The preservation witnesses are respectively the checked normalization derivation, finite ancestor marginalization identity, checked district sum-product derivation, admissible extraction equations \(A_Dq_D^\star=m_D\), active-face calculation, finite additivity, and district factorization. The \(\mathsf{CONDITION}\) rule labels its terminal with the same two root values and divides only under an independent strict-positivity certificate. In the rank \(\operatorname{rank}_{\mathrm{lex}}=(r_N,r_A,r_S,r_X,r_F,r_{\Sigma},r_{\Pi},r_C)\), the first seven rules respectively decrease \(r_N,r_A,r_S,r_X,r_F,r_{\Sigma},r_{\Pi}\) while fixing every earlier coordinate, and \(\mathsf{CONDITION}\) decreases \(r_C\) after the others vanish; no rule creates an earlier-phase node. The fixed priority and least-applicable-node convention give a unique successor. From a well-typed initial configuration, \(\operatorname{STUCK}\) is unreachable because every declared partial-operation failure takes its specified \(\operatorname{FAIL}\) branch.
statements.justification: A typed operational semantics needs a local invariant for every transition before terminal soundness follows.
statements.gap: The prior transport recursions prove their own rule systems sound, but do not cover certified Layer-3 extraction from heterogeneous source-labelled laws.
statements.consumer: The local invariant supports independent checking of a returned derivation or failure trace.

statements.statement: For every realizable typed menu with \(\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\ne\varnothing\), the priority transition system \(\mathsf{DCTFTR}\) has a unique finite run because \(\operatorname{rank}_{\mathrm{lex}}\in\mathbb N^8\) decreases lexicographically. Every reached configuration has root denotation \((P_{M^\star}(B_\rho\wedge E),P_{M^\star}(E))\) for every \(\mathbf M\in\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\). If the result is \(\operatorname{ID}(\operatorname{Quot}(F_B,F_E,\pi),\delta_B,\delta_E,\pi)\), then \(F_B,F_E\in\mathscr R(\mathcal P)\), \(\pi\) proves \(F_E>0\) throughout \(\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\), and \(F_B(\mathcal P)/F_E(\mathcal P)=Q_\rho^\star(\mathbf M)\) for every compatible model. If \(z\) proves \(F_E=0\) throughout the fiber, the result is \(\operatorname{ZERO\_EVIDENCE}(F_E,z)\) and the conditional is undefined. A split failure, failed extraction, normalization-only face failure, denominator witness at zero, or uncertified denominator positivity returns its typed \(\operatorname{FAIL}\) trace and performs no division. A \(\operatorname{FACE\_NOT\_IDENTIFIED}\) witness certifies only local district-face variation and implies global nonidentification only when the hypotheses of the one-district fiber-projection theorem are separately verified. The observed numerical sign of \(F_E\) is never itself a positivity certificate, and \(\operatorname{STUCK}\) is unreachable from a well-typed initial configuration.
statements.justification: The source-labelled Layer-3 recursion must be valid before its output can enter the sharper arm-ordering analysis.
statements.gap: CTFTR handles heterogeneous Layer-1/2 inputs and CTFIDU+ handles one-specification Layer-3 inputs; neither soundness argument covers both features simultaneously.
statements.consumer: A successful output can be evaluated directly from released source tables, while impossible conditioning events are rejected before division.

statements.statement: Under the finite semi-Markovian convention, the observational and atomic hard-interventional restriction \(\mathfrak I_{\mathrm{CTFTR}}\) has a proper typed embedding into \(\mathfrak I_{\mathrm{DCTFTR}}\). The DCTFTR-expressible intersection \(\mathfrak I_{\mathrm{CTFIDU+}}\) of the published one-SCM Layer-3 grammar has a proper typed embedding obtained by setting \(\mathcal S=\{\star\}\) and applying its declared constructor map. No embedding of the full CTFTR conditional or stochastic-policy grammar, and no embedding of an undeclared CTFIDU+ Layer-2.5 action, is asserted. On either embedded restriction, every successful DCTFTR functional and every successful functional returned by the corresponding published calculus equals the same causal query in every compatible model; syntactic or transition-by-transition equivalence is not asserted. In \(\mathfrak I_{\mathrm{bin}}\), the first restriction cannot accept the genuine cross-world cell \(p\), while the complete source-labelled family with \(P^\star(Z=1)=0\) and \(P^s(Z=1)=1\) is not realizable by one SCM and hence is outside the second restriction.
statements.justification: Typed proper embeddings state exactly which published input classes are recovered and where the multi-domain Layer-3 language is strictly larger.
statements.gap: CTFTR and CTFIDU+ occupy different proper subgrammars; neither accepts the complete binary multi-domain instance.
statements.consumer: Users can recognize settled CTFTR and CTFIDU+ cases while reserving DCTFTR for genuinely heterogeneous Layer-3 inputs.

statements.statement:
Suppose \(\mathcal K_D(m_D)\ne\varnothing\) and \(d_Dq>0\) for every \(q\in\mathcal K_D(m_D)\). Then
\[
\Gamma_{\rho\prec\sigma}(m_D)=
\max_{\eta\in\mathbb R^{\operatorname{rows}(A_D)}}
\{m_D^\top\eta:A_D^\top\eta\le g_{\rho,\sigma,D}^\top\}.
\]
Every feasible dual vector with \(m_D^\top\eta>0\) certifies \(Q_\sigma^\star>Q_\rho^\star\) in every model in the broad fiber \(\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\). If additionally \(\mathsf{BASep}_D(\mathcal P)\) holds, this certificate condition is also necessary for uniform strict dominance on the focal-district-saturated fiber. Under this additional hypothesis, \(\Gamma_{\rho\prec\sigma}(m_D)<0\) is attained by an original-alphabet compatible focal-district-saturated SCM with \(Q_\sigma^\star<Q_\rho^\star\), and \(\Gamma_{\rho\prec\sigma}(m_D)<0<\overline\Gamma_{\rho\prec\sigma}(m_D)\) yields two such SCM families with opposite strict rankings while preserving every other district's graph-compatible restrictions. Nonemptiness of \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)\) together with \(\mathsf{ASep}_D(\mathcal P)\), and hence with \(\mathsf{Sep}_D(\mathcal P)\), is sufficient for the exact clauses. Without baseline-averaged focal projection, the primal optimizers need not lift from the row face.
statements.justification: The theorem gives an auditable broad-fiber dual certificate and exact opposing focal SCMs under the sharp single-baseline projection condition.
statements.gap: Transported bandit results do not derive this heterogeneous Layer-3 dual certificate or baseline-averaged fixed-alphabet countermodel lift.
statements.consumer: A bandit analyst can audit strict removal by source-table weights and lift a reversing optimizer without altering any nonfocal district.

statements.statement: Suppose \(\mathcal K_D(m_D)\ne\varnothing\) and \(d_Dq>0\) throughout \(\mathcal K_D(m_D)\). For every realizable additional row \(r_D^\dagger\), the feasible set \(I_D\) is a closed interval and \(p\mapsto\Gamma_{\rho\prec\sigma}(p;m_D)\) is a finite convex piecewise-affine function. Its pieces may be obtained from feasible bases of the row-augmented dual program and have coefficients that are rational affine functions of \(m_D\). Hence \(\mathcal J_{\rho\prec\sigma}^+\) is the complement in \(I_D\) of a closed convex subset, which is empty, a point, or a closed interval, and has zero, one, or two relative sign boundaries. Each boundary has a dual menu-weight certificate of value zero and a primal row-face law attaining equality; the adjacent strict-pruning side has a positive dual piece. If the supplied menu augmented by the boundary equality \(r_D^\dagger q=p\) satisfies its \(\mathsf{BASep}_D\) predicate, the equality law is realized by an SCM saturated only at \(D\) on the original alphabets \(\mathcal X\), with every district \(D'\ne D\) retaining its original graph-compatible restrictions. Nonemptiness of the augmented focal-district-saturated compatibility fiber together with its \(\mathsf{ASep}_D\) predicate, and hence with its \(\mathsf{Sep}_D\) predicate, is sufficient for that boundary realization. Without baseline-averaged focal projection, no SCM lifting of the row-face boundary is asserted.
statements.justification: This gives the exact parametric Layer-3 sign boundary and realizes boundary laws under the augmented menu's sharp single-baseline condition.
statements.gap: Existing fixed-menu and bandit results do not give a parametric Layer-3 cell diagram with baseline-averaged focal boundary SCMs.
statements.consumer: A study designer can locate pruning regions and obtain a boundary SCM whenever one compatible baseline preserves the augmented menu.

statements.statement: For \(\mathfrak I_{\mathrm{bin}}\), the base face has the unique parameterization \(q(p)=(p,1/2-p,1/2-p,p)\), \(0\le p\le1/2\), and \[Q_\rho(q(p))=1-2p,\qquad Q_\sigma(q(p))=1/2,\qquad I_D=[0,1/2],\qquad \Gamma_{\rho\prec\sigma}(p;m_D)=2p-1/2,\qquad \mathcal J_{\rho\prec\sigma}^+=(1/4,1/2].\] With the augmented row order consisting of the three rows of \(A_D\) followed by \(r_D^\dagger\), the dual vector \((0,-1,0,2)^\top\) represents \(g_{\rho,\sigma,D}\) exactly and has value \(2p-1/2\); at the realized value \(p=3/8\) it certifies margin \(1/4\). The boundary SCM is \(q(1/4)=(1/4,1/4,1/4,1/4)\), while \(q(0)\) makes \(\rho\) strictly optimal and \(q(1/2)\) makes \(\sigma\) strictly optimal on the original binary alphabets. For the sole unit-cost block, \[\operatorname{PO}(\varnothing)=\{\rho,\sigma\},\qquad \mathcal K_{\{e^\dagger\}}=\{q(3/8)\},\qquad \operatorname{PO}(\{e^\dagger\})=\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}}=\{\sigma\}.\] The first equality is witnessed by \(p=0\) for \(\rho\) and \(p=1/2\) for \(\sigma\); at \(p=3/8\), \(Q_\sigma=1/2>1/4=Q_\rho\), and no other arm exists because \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{arm}}=\{\rho,\sigma\}\).
statements.justification: This exhaustive binary calculation verifies the sign frontier, the dual certificate, the boundary law, and the decision consequence in one complete instance.
statements.gap: The published identification and bandit papers do not exhibit a heterogeneous genuine Layer-3 cell whose observed value crosses an exact transported pruning boundary.
statements.consumer: The instance is a regression test for extraction, face identification, experiment blocking, and undefined-arm-safe pruning.

statements.statement: Suppose the reduced arm comparison has one district \(D\). If there exists \(\eta_{\rho,\sigma,D}\) with \(A_D^\top\eta_{\rho,\sigma,D}\le g_{\rho,\sigma,D}^\top\) and \(m_D^\top\eta_{\rho,\sigma,D}>0\), removing \(\rho\) cannot remove a maximizing arm from \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{arm}}\); an arm whose common evidence is certified zero is excluded as undefined rather than ranked.
statements.justification: This records the elementary decision consequence while keeping it out of the research kernel.
statements.gap: The exclusion rule itself is elementary and is not positioned as a strengthening of Park and Lee; the new content is the derived sharp certificate in Theorems 5 and 6.
statements.consumer: A counterfactual bandit can initialize exploration on the certificate-retained action set without treating undefined conditionals as low rewards.

statements.statement:
Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{r\times N}\), \(m\in\mathbb R^r\), and \(c\in\mathbb R^N\). If \(K=\{q\in\mathbb R^N:q\geq0,\ Aq=m\}\) is nonempty and bounded, then both optima are attained and
\[
 \min_{q\in K}c^\top q
 =\max_{\eta\in\mathbb R^r}\{m^\top\eta:A^\top\eta\leq c\}.
\]

source.verbatim_statement: Theorem 4.4 (Strong duality) If a linear programming problem has an optimal solution, so does its dual, and the respective optimal costs are equal.

attestation.note: Exact theorem statement transcribed from Bertsimas and Tsitsiklis, Introduction to Linear Optimization (1997), Chapter 4, p. 148; publisher handle https://athenasc.com/linoptbook.html, corroborated against the web-visible book scan.

statements.statement: For every instance in the observational and hard-interventional CTFTR input class, if the published CTFTR algorithm returns an expression for a conditional counterfactual query, that expression equals the query in every causal model compatible with the input instance.

source.verbatim_statement: Theorem 5.1 (CTFTR completeness). A counterfactual probability P*(y* | x*) is transportable from Z and G_Delta if and only if CTFTR returns an expression for it.

attestation.note: Exact theorem statement transcribed from the authors' PMLR source-of-record PDF, page 20 (paper pagination), https://proceedings.mlr.press/v162/correa22a/correa22a.pdf; notation normalized only to plain-text ASCII.

statements.statement: For every one-specification instance with realizable unnested Layer-3 input distributions, if the published CTFIDU+ algorithm returns an expression for the target counterfactual, that expression equals the target in every causal model compatible with the input instance.

source.verbatim_statement: Theorem 3.5 (CTFIDU+ soundness and completeness). Given an un-nested counterfactual expression Y*, P(Y*=y) is identifiable from a causal diagram G and a set of input distributions A, iff CTFIDU+ returns an expression for it.

attestation.note: Exact theorem statement transcribed from the authors' arXiv v2 source-of-record PDF, page 6, https://arxiv.org/pdf/2602.23541v2; notation normalized only to plain-text ASCII.

statements.statement: For every finite-state recursive SCM \(M^s\) compatible with \(G\) on \(\mathcal X\), there is a finite canonical SCM \(N^s\) with the same causal diagram and the same observed state spaces such that every finite joint counterfactual distribution induced by \(N^s\) equals the corresponding distribution induced by \(M^s\).

source.locator: Theorem 2.4, page 3, lines 246--251 of the PMLR PDF
source.verbatim_statement: For any set of counterfactual variables \(Y_x,\ldots,Z_w\), \(P_M(Y_x,\ldots,Z_w)=P_N(Y_x,\ldots,Z_w)\).

attestation.note: Transcribed from Zhang, Tian, and Bareinboim (2022), Theorem 2.4(2), and checked together with clause (1), which states that the original and canonical SCMs have the same causal diagram.

statements.justification: This published canonicalization theorem is the finite-support substrate adapted here domain by domain and synchronized across invariant districts.
statements.gap: The source theorem is one-domain; it does not itself impose source labels, district invariance, complete Layer-3 menu constraints, or the fixed-alphabet multi-domain optimization fiber.
statements.consumer: The exact global canonical-frontier theorem uses it to replace each compatible source SCM without changing supplied or target counterfactual cells.

statements.statement: Over an effectively presented real algebraic coefficient field, cylindrical algebraic decomposition terminates on every finite first-order formula built from polynomial sign conditions, returns an equivalent quantifier-free formula, and constructs a finite sign-invariant cylindrical cell decomposition with algebraic sample points for its nonempty cells.  Projection polynomials, isolating data, lifted sign tables, and sample points provide finite exact certificates for the returned truth values and witnesses.

source.locator: Chapters 13 and 16, Cylindrical Decomposition Algorithm and Quantifier Elimination

attestation.note: Stable publisher DOI and chapter locators supplied because a lawful theorem-level transcription was not available.

statements.statement: For every finite first-order formula over an effectively presented real-algebraic coefficient field, Collins's cylindrical algebraic decomposition algorithm terminates, constructs finitely many sign-invariant cylindrical cells with exact real-algebraic sample points, and returns a quantifier-free formula equivalent to the input formula.  The projection polynomials, isolating data, lifted sign tables, sample points, and the truth-value propagation provide finite exact verification data.

source.locator: Section 2, Theorems 1--3 and Algorithm QE by CAD, pp. 10--13

attestation.note: Transcribed from Collins (1998), Section 2, Theorem 3; the cited adjacent Theorems 1--2 and displayed QE-by-CAD algorithm specify cell evaluation at sample points, propagation, and the finite construction.

statements.statement: For every finite set \(\mathcal P_0\) of polynomials in \(R[X_1,\ldots,X_k]\), there is a cylindrical decomposition of \(R^k\) adapted to \(\mathcal P_0\), and such a decomposition can be computed in time \((sd)^{2^{O(k)}}\), where \(s=\operatorname{card}\mathcal P_0\) and \(d=\max_{P\in\mathcal P_0}\deg(P)\).

source.verbatim_statement: For every finite set \(P\) of polynomials in \(R[X_1,\ldots,X_k]\), there is a cylindrical decomposition of \(R^k\) adapted to \(P\). Moreover, such a decomposition can be computed in time \((sd)^{2^{O(k)}}\), where \(s=\operatorname{card} P\) and \(d=\max_{P\in P}\deg(P)\).

attestation.note: Transcribed from the author-hosted paper, Theorem 2.4, p. 6; used only for adapted cylindrical decomposition and its effective computation.

source.verbatim_statement: Let P \(\subset R[X^{[1]},\ldots,X^{[\omega]},Y]_{\le d}\) be a finite set of s polynomials, where \(X^{[i]}\) is a block of \(k_i\) variables, and Y is a block of \(\ell\) variables. Consider the quantified formula \(\Psi(Y)=(Q_1X^{[1]})\cdots(Q_\omega X^{[\omega]})\Phi(X^{[1]},\ldots,X^{[\omega]},Y)\), where \(\Phi\) is a quantifier-free P-formula. Then there exists a quantifier-free formula \(\Theta(Y)=\bigvee_{i=1}^{I}\bigwedge_{j=1}^{J_i}\bigvee_{n=1}^{N_{ij}}\operatorname{sign}(P_{ijn}(Y))=\sigma_{ijn}\) equivalent to \(\Psi\), where \(P_{ijn}(Y)\) are polynomials in the variables Y and \(\sigma_{ijn}\in\{-1,0,1\}\). Furthermore, \(I\le s^{(k_\omega+1)\cdots(k_1+1)(\ell+1)}d^{O(k_\omega)\cdots O(k_1)O(\ell)}\), \(J_i\le s^{(k_\omega+1)\cdots(k_1+1)}d^{O(k_\omega)\cdots O(k_1)}\), \(N_{ij}\le d^{O(k_\omega)\cdots O(k_1)}\), and the degrees of the polynomials \(P_{ijn}(y)\) are bounded by \(d^{O(k_\omega)\cdots O(k_1)}\). Moreover, there exists an algorithm ([5, Algorithm 14.5] (Quantifier Elimination)) to compute \(\Theta(Y)\) with complexity \(s^{(k_\omega+1)\cdots(k_1+1)(\ell+1)}d^{O(k_\omega)\cdots O(k_1)O(\ell)}\) in D, where D denotes the ring generated by the coefficients of the polynomials in P. If D = Z and \(\tau\) denotes an upper bound on bitsizes of P, then the bitsizes of the integers in the intermediate computations and the output are bounded by \(\tau d^{O(k_\omega)\cdots O(k_1)O(\ell)}\).

attestation.note: Transcribed from the source-of-record repository copy, Section 4.1.2, Theorem 3, pp. 10--11; used only for effective equivalent quantifier-free output and its displayed arithmetic bound.

statements.statement: Under the frozen transport assumptions, district closure has no nontrivial strictly weaker graph-only replacement for a partially selected district.  More precisely, omit district closure while retaining district-kernel invariance exactly as stated, and let \(0<|D\cap\Delta_s|<|D|\).  Then every nonconstant binary incidence row on \(\Omega_D\) admits two finite original-alphabet SCM families having identical supplied source laws but different target values of that row.  Hence, based on a source row alone, the universally transportable rows are exactly the constant rows.  If one additionally assumes invariance of the marginal response law on \(I=D\setminus\Delta_s\), then a row transports for every compatible pair if and only if it is constant on every fiber of the coordinate projection \(\Omega_D\to\Omega_I\); this condition is decidable by finite enumeration, and failure gives a two-point leakage certificate.

For every district \(D\),
\[
\mathsf{Sep}_D(\mathcal P)\Longrightarrow\mathsf{ASep}_D(\mathcal P).
\]
The implication is strict in general.  In particular, take two independent binary response coordinates \(Y_0\) and \(Z\) generated by distinct singleton districts, let \(D\) be the district generating \(Y_0\), and supply in the target domain both the complete marginal law of \(Y_0\) and the complete joint law of \((Y_0,Z)\).  The resulting menu satisfies \(\mathsf{ASep}_D(\mathcal P)\) but not \(\mathsf{Sep}_D(\mathcal P)\).

For every district \(D\),
\[
\bigl\{\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)\ne\varnothing
\text{ and }\mathsf{ASep}_D(\mathcal P)\bigr\}
\Longrightarrow \mathsf{BASep}_D(\mathcal P).
\]
Together with \(\mathsf{Sep}_D(\mathcal P)\Longrightarrow\mathsf{ASep}_D(\mathcal P)\), this gives the convenient hierarchy
\[
\bigl\{\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)\ne\varnothing
\text{ and }\mathsf{Sep}_D(\mathcal P)\bigr\}
\Longrightarrow
\bigl\{\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)\ne\varnothing
\text{ and }\mathsf{ASep}_D(\mathcal P)\bigr\}
\Longrightarrow \mathsf{BASep}_D(\mathcal P).
\]
The second implication is strict on finite original alphabets: there is a three-vertex binary DAG and a complete target-domain menu for which \(\mathsf{BASep}_D(\mathcal P)\) holds but \(\mathsf{ASep}_D(\mathcal P)\) fails because two Boolean focal slices outside \(R_D(m_D)\) average to a row inside it under the witnessing nonfocal product law.
statements.justification: This hierarchy makes the sharp single-baseline preservation premise explicit while retaining two increasingly simple sufficient checks.
statements.gap: Pointwise active-slice control is stronger than the fixed-baseline construction needs because only averages under the frozen nonfocal product law enter complete-cell probabilities.
statements.consumer: The focal projection theorem and its identification, dominance, frontier, and global corollaries use baseline-averaged separation for exact lifting.

statements.statement:
For every finite instance, all minimum-cost Layer-3 regime-block solutions are characterized by enumerating \(S\subseteq\mathcal U\) and, for each arm, solving the finite linear program consisting of the equations defining \(\mathcal K_S\), the common-denominator positivity test, and the pairwise numerator-gap inequalities. This is an algorithmic computation whenever all matrix entries, menu values, and costs are effectively presented rational or real algebraic numbers. In general the elimination function \(f\) is not submodular. In particular, there is a realizable one-domain binary one-district instance with two unit-cost Layer-3 cell experiments for which
\[
\operatorname{PO}(\varnothing)=\operatorname{PO}(\{e_1\})
=\operatorname{PO}(\{e_2\})=\{\rho,\sigma\},
\qquad
\operatorname{PO}(\{e_1,e_2\})=\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}}=\{\sigma\}.
\]
Consequently the marginal gain of \(e_2\) is zero at \(S=\varnothing\) and one at \(T_{\mathrm{exp}}=\{e_1\}\), violating diminishing returns. For this instance the exact acquisition problem is
\[
\min_{x_1,x_2\in\{0,1\}}x_1+x_2
\quad\text{subject to}\quad x_1+x_2\geq2,
\]
whose unique solution is \((x_1,x_2)=(1,1)\) with cost two. The multiplier \(y=1\) for the covering inequality is a matching dual lower-bound certificate for the continuous relaxation.

There are two exact finite frontiers with different scopes.

First, assume \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat}}(\mathcal P)\ne\varnothing\). Then \(\Theta(\mathcal P)\) is a nonempty compact semialgebraic set and, for every finite collection \(\mathcal F\) of declared target-domain counterfactual cells,
\[
\{(P_{M^\star}(C):C\in\mathcal F):\mathbf M\in\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat}}(\mathcal P)\}
=
\{(\Psi_C^\star(\theta^\star):C\in\mathcal F):\theta\in\Theta(\mathcal P)\}.
\]
Every \(\Psi_C^s\) is multi-affine in the district response-law blocks and has total degree at most the number of districts visited by \(C\). Every point of the right-hand range is realized by a district-saturated SCM family on the original observed alphabets \(\mathcal X\).

Second, for an arbitrary acyclic directed mixed graph, if \(\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\ne\varnothing\), then \(\Theta_G^{\mathrm{can}}(\mathcal P)\) is a nonempty compact semialgebraic set and
\[
\{(P_{M^\star}(C):C\in\mathcal F):\mathbf M\in\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\}
=
\{(\Phi_{C,\mathrm{can}}^\star(\vartheta^\star):C\in\mathcal F):
\vartheta\in\Theta_G^{\mathrm{can}}(\mathcal P)\}.
\]
The canonical realization also uses the original observed alphabets and retains the internal latent-factor restrictions of \(G\).

For either exact row
\[
(\mathfrak C,\Lambda,\Xi)
\in
\{(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat}}(\mathcal P),\Theta(\mathcal P),\Psi),
(\mathcal C(\mathcal P),\Theta_G^{\mathrm{can}}(\mathcal P),\Phi_{\mathrm{can}})\},
\]
provided \(\mathfrak C\ne\varnothing\), the quantities
\[
\min_{x\in\Lambda}\Xi_T^\star(x^\star)
\quad\text{and}\quad
\max_{x\in\Lambda}\Xi_T^\star(x^\star)
\]
are respectively the attained sharp lower and upper bounds for the target cell. At least one bound is strictly inside the logical interval \([0,1]\) exactly when the lower endpoint is positive or the upper endpoint is less than one, and the cell is identified exactly when the two extrema agree. If the extrema differ, minimizing and maximizing realizations give two original-alphabet same-menu SCM families attaining different endpoint values. No assertion is made that every scalar value between the two extrema is attained. These are finite semialgebraic characterizations.

For the same row let
\[
e_-(\Lambda)=\min_{x\in\Lambda}\Xi_E^\star(x^\star),
\qquad e_+(\Lambda)=\max_{x\in\Lambda}\Xi_E^\star(x^\star).
\]
If \(e_+(\Lambda)=0\), evidence is zero throughout \(\mathfrak C\); if \(e_-(\Lambda)=0<e_+(\Lambda)\), positivity is not uniform. In either case a conditional functional on all of \(\mathfrak C\) is rejected before division. If \(e_-(\Lambda)>0\), the quantities
\[
\min_{x\in\Lambda}
\frac{\Xi_{B_\rho\cap E}^\star(x^\star)}{\Xi_E^\star(x^\star)}
\quad\text{and}\quad
\max_{x\in\Lambda}
\frac{\Xi_{B_\rho\cap E}^\star(x^\star)}{\Xi_E^\star(x^\star)}
\]
are the attained sharp lower and upper conditional bounds. If they differ, their endpoint models are distinct; no interval-filling property of the conditional image is asserted. Under this positivity condition, \(Q_\sigma^\star>Q_\rho^\star\) throughout \(\mathfrak C\) if and only if
\[
\min_{x\in\Lambda}
\{\Xi_{B_\sigma\cap E}^\star(x^\star)-\Xi_{B_\rho\cap E}^\star(x^\star)\}>0,
\]
and opposite strict rankings occur in two same-menu original-alphabet models if and only if the minimum of the displayed gap is negative and its maximum is positive. Thus this strict minimum is the exact safe-pruning certificate for the chosen fiber.

Finally, for every district \(D\),
\[
\mathcal Q_D(\mathcal P)\subseteq\mathcal K_D(m_D).
\]
If \(\mathsf{BASep}_D(\mathcal P)\) holds, the one-district fiber-projection theorem gives the exact local equality
\[
\mathcal Q_D^{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)=\mathcal K_D(m_D),
\]
and \(\mathsf{BASep}_D(\mathcal P)\) itself entails a nonempty focal-district-saturated compatibility fiber. This equality requires saturation only of the focal district and preserves the graph-compatible restrictions of every \(D'\ne D\). Cross-district coupling of a complete supplied cell is harmless for the fixed-baseline replacement exactly when its baseline-averaged focal row lies in \(R_D(m_D)\), because
\[
R_D(m_D)=\operatorname{span}\{q-q':q,q'\in\mathcal K_D(m_D)\}^{\perp}.
\]
Nonemptiness of \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)\) together with \(\mathsf{ASep}_D(\mathcal P)\), and hence with \(\mathsf{Sep}_D(\mathcal P)\), is a baseline-free sufficient certificate for this equality. The baseline-averaged predicate is generally baseline-dependent and not directly checkable from menu cells alone; allowing a different baseline for each candidate \(q\) is not asserted. Outside focal-district saturation and baseline-averaged separation, \(\mathcal K_D(m_D)\) is certified only as an outer relaxation. This local equality is distinct from the first, all-district-saturated global row, whose Cartesian district variation makes the multi-affine program exact. Consequently a failed local face test is not a global nonidentification certificate outside the focal projection theorem's scope; distinct endpoint optimizers of the appropriate exact global program are the paired-model certificate whenever their objective values differ.
statements.justification: The theorem separates exact all-district multi-affine variation, exact sparse canonical optimization, and exact single-baseline focal-district geometry.
statements.gap: Global programs retain every cross-district polynomial equality; locally, a weaker baseline-averaged condition preserves those cells than pointwise active-slice control.
statements.consumer: Global bounds and pruning use exact endpoint optimizers, while local LP certificates use focal saturation plus baseline-averaged separation or its baseline-free sufficient checks.

statements.statement: Assume \(\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\ne\varnothing\) and that every supplied menu probability is effectively presented as a rational or real-algebraic number.  For either an unconditional finite target-domain counterfactual cell \(T\) or the conditional query \(Q_\rho^\star=P_{M^\star}(B_\rho\mid E)\), the proof-producing algorithm \(\mathsf{DCTFTR\text{-}CAN}\) has a unique finite run and returns exactly one sound terminal.  A successful fast-path terminal \(\operatorname{ID\_RAT}(F,\delta)\) satisfies \(F\in\mathscr R(\mathcal P)\) and equals the causal query throughout \(\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\).  Otherwise the exact canonical fallback is exhaustive: for an unconditional query it returns \(\operatorname{ID\_CAN}\) exactly when the sharp canonical extrema agree and otherwise returns \(\operatorname{PAIR\_CAN}\) with two original-alphabet same-menu SCM families attaining unequal endpoint probabilities.  For a conditional query it returns \(\operatorname{ZERO\_EVIDENCE}\) exactly when the maximum compatible evidence probability is zero; it returns \(\operatorname{NOT\_UNIFORMLY\_DEFINED}\) when the minimum is zero and the maximum is positive, with respective zero- and positive-evidence witnesses; and only when the minimum evidence probability is strictly positive does it optimize the conditional ratio, returning \(\operatorname{ID\_CAN}\) exactly when its sharp extrema agree and otherwise \(\operatorname{PAIR\_CAN}\) with two original-alphabet same-menu SCM families attaining unequal conditional values.  Every global certificate and witness is checkable by exact real-algebraic arithmetic.  Thus every unresolved local \(\mathsf{DCTFTR}\) trace is completed by an exact fixed-declared-alphabet identification, undefinedness, or paired-model certificate; a local face failure alone is never treated as broad-model nonidentification.

statements.statement: Every finite fixing trace accepted by the extraction calculus preserves the represented event probability.  More precisely, if the trace expands its input and output into finite response-profile expressions, uses division only by a separately certified positive context probability, and its exact checker verifies the cleared-denominator polynomial identity, then the input and output expressions agree in every \(\mathbf M\in\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\).

Every checked derivation \(\delta:A\Downarrow F\) in the finite extraction calculus satisfies
\[
F(\mathcal P)=P_{M^s}(A)
\]
for every \(\mathbf M\in\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\).  Every accepted positivity certificate is valid on its declared compatibility fiber.  Moreover, \(\operatorname{SupportLocal}_D(A)\) terminates and accepts if and only if the recursive indicator of \(A\) is independent of the nonfocal response profiles; upon acceptance its constructed row \(\operatorname{row}_D(A)\) equals that indicator for every nonfocal profile.

For every finite first-order formula over an effectively presented real-algebraic coefficient field, the fixed builder in \(\mathrm{def:hybrid\text{-}result\text{-}grammar}\) terminates and produces an \(\mathsf{AlgTrace}\) accepted by \(\operatorname{CheckAlg}\).  Every accepted trace has the following sound semantics: its output formula is equivalent to its input; its cells cover the represented real space and carry the displayed constant signs; its quantified truth table is correct; and every reported algebraic sample satisfies its displayed cell constraints.  If \(S\) is a nonempty compact semialgebraic set and \(p,q\) are polynomials with \(q>0\) on \(S\), the optimization traces for \(p\) and \(p/q\) return the exact attained lower and upper endpoints and feasible attaining samples.  These claims are verified from the trace by finite integer and rational arithmetic; no cited result is used for sample semantics, truth propagation, endpoint selection, or witness lifting.

sampling_model.design: Exact population laws from finite source-labelled menus of observational, hard-interventional, and declared realizable partial-copy regimes.
sampling_model.units: Each law is generated by independent units from its domain-specific finite recursive SCM; identification is at the population-law level.
sampling_model.treatment: Treatments and partial-copy operations are fixed by descriptor \(a\), and source shifts are encoded by \(\Delta_s\).
sampling_model.overlap: No blanket positivity assumption is imposed. The recursion returns \(\operatorname{ZERO\_EVIDENCE}(F_E,z)\) for an identified zero evidence probability, and arm-order theorems explicitly restrict to a face on which the common evidence row is positive.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: No nuisance estimator enters the identification claim; finite-sample estimation of returned functionals and dual margins is downstream.

tldr: Heterogeneous sites can supply genuine Layer-3 partial-copy laws. A certified extraction judgment turns each available context and cell into a typed district row only after source admissibility is proved. On a fixed-alphabet one-district compatibility face, the sharp transported arm-gap equals an explicit dual weighting of all retained source-labelled cells, and an added Layer-3 regime block yields a finite piecewise-affine pruning frontier. DCTFTR is an inductive, terminating transition system with typed failures and zero-evidence rejection. A complete binary instance gives the margin \(2p-1/2\), while minimum-cost regime-block acquisition and multi-district face preservation remain explicit open questions.

project_justification.gap: CTFTR transports conditional counterfactuals from heterogeneous Layer-1/2 inputs, CTFIDU+ identifies from Layer-3 inputs in one causal specification, and Park--Lee pruning uses graph-based action classes or fixed transported bounds. None derives an exact source-menu certificate or a sign-regime boundary for the order of conditional Layer-3 arms.
project_justification.niche: District-closed shifts and common-evidence arm comparisons reduce one confounded target block to a boundary-sensitive response polytope. Its LP dual converts released source cells into an auditable ranking certificate, while a candidate menu value parametrizes a genuine pruning phase transition.
project_justification.fill: The project proves fixed-alphabet realization of the compatible face, gives certified typed extraction and an inductive DCTFTR semantics, replaces global row span by an active-face criterion, derives sharp primal--dual arm-order certificates, verifies the complete binary phase boundary, and poses minimum-cost regime-block acquisition before asking whether the construction survives multi-district gluing.

related_work: Correa, Lee, and Bareinboim (2022, Theorem 5.1) supply the source-labelled conditional transport architecture for Layers 1 and 2; Proposition 1 proves proper typed inclusion of their problem-instance subgrammar and sound semantic agreement of successful functionals, without asserting syntactic or transition-level equivalence. Raghavan and Bareinboim (2026, Theorem 3.5 and Appendix E.1) supply Layer-3 factor extraction and ctf-thickets for one causal specification; Proposition 1 embeds that setting through \(\mathcal S=\{\star\}\) and proves non-representability of the complete binary multi-domain instance, without claiming that its scalar cell alone is outside CTFIDU+. Zhang, Tian, and Bareinboim (2022, Theorem 2.4) supply the finite response carrier, and Choe et al. (2026, Proposition 3.1) motivate preserving all information rows; both inform rather than serve as tightening targets. Bareinboim and Pearl (2012, Theorems 5--7) and Bareinboim and Pearl (2014) supply vertex-level selection diagrams and multi-environment completeness, whereas district joint-kernel invariance is a stronger Layer-3 transport condition. Park and Lee (2026, ICLR, Theorems 1--3) define realizable Layer-3 action classes, and Park and Lee (2026, UAI, Theorems 1--2) give valid Layer-1/2 transported bandit bounds; they inform the menu-dual order certificate, binary pruning boundary, and ex-post block-acquisition question rather than serving as results claimed to be beaten.
technical_internal_limitation: Boundary fibers require the active normals \(e_\omega\) for \(\omega\in Z_D(m_D)\); ordinary row span alone can miss identification when the menu forces response profiles to zero. Multi-district completeness is not asserted. The smallest binary two-hedge thicket must compare every recursive failure with target-score constancy on the exact global compatibility fiber; a failed recursion with a constant target would redirect the global claim to sharp polynomial transported bounds.
honest_scope: The face projection, active-face identification criterion, dual arm-order theorem, one-cell phase diagram, and complete binary check concern a reduced one-district comparison with common positive evidence. DCTFTR soundness covers broader district-closed instances, but fixed-cardinality multi-district completeness is open. The acquisition objective is finite and ex post; it is not an ex-ante adaptive policy. No assumption supplies the dominance margin, active face, or threshold. The observational and hard-interventional problem-instance subgrammar is properly included in DCTFTR and successful outputs agree semantically with the target, the one-domain problem-instance class includes the CTFIDU+ setting, and sure evidence reduces conditional arm order to the unconditional numerator-gap program.
